summary: YNAB ZIP importer: local preview/atomic import and a complete ordered CLI migration workflow, including classification, optional shared Plaid setup and six-hour updates.

operations.name: import.workflow
operations.summary:
YNAB migration: eight reviewed stages

Guide prerequisites: CLI 2.10+ and WHAB 2.64+; optional shared-bank stages
use Plaid 1.8+. These guide prerequisites do not change SDK parser compatibility.

This is an ordered guide, not one script to run blindly. It is documentation,
not an executable import.workflow command or an invocation of FileImport.parse.
Complete and verify each stage before continuing. If the destination already
exists or is partly migrated, resume from its actual state; do not recreate,
reset or reimport it. Start with whab budget list and account list as needed.

All names, files, dates and IDs below are fictional. Replace migration-example
with your permanent destination budget's observed name or ID; quote names with
spaces/emoji/non-Latin text. Replace export.zip with your chosen local export.
Uppercase CONNECTION_ID, BANK_ACCOUNT_ID, WHAB_ACCOUNT_ID and
SHA256_FROM_PREVIEW are placeholders, never literal values to submit.
Configured local defaults are used: do not repeat --home or --environment
production routinely. Production is the CLI default. For development, use an
isolated fictional runtime with explicit --home and --environment sandbox;
never use household data as a fixture. Help and offline discovery open no host.

1. Create or select the permanent destination
Purpose: keep the migration in the intended durable budget, with no staging
ledger that must later be renamed or copied.
  whab budget list
  whab budget create migration-example
  whab migration-example plugin enable ynab-zip-importer
  whab migration-example plugin status
Optional visual interface:
  whab migration-example plugin enable web
Inspect the returned budget id/name and configured/active plugin selections.
Creation makes an empty SQLite budget with default category templates, no bank
connections and no inherited financial data. Existing files/duplicate names
are refused. If the budget already exists, select it and skip create. If a
plugin change reports restart_required, apply its reported restart requirement
through your normal host/launcher controls and verify status before continuing.
Web is optional; its successful enable result supplies host_url. Browser TLS
trust is a separate explicit setup choice. No YNAB login or token is needed.
Decision: confirm this permanent destination before selecting any export.

2. Preview the chosen export, then commit exactly the reviewed file
Purpose: inspect the file's interpretation before the atomic import.
  whab migration-example import ynab preview '~/Downloads/export.zip' --currency USD
Inspect fingerprint, accounts/categories/transactions/assignments counts,
warnings, canImport, reason and alreadyImported. Confirm the file's monetary
values are USD; a dollar sign alone does not establish currency. The ZIP must
be nonempty and at most 10 MiB. CLI import targets the named pristine personal
budget: no existing accounts, transactions or assignments. It never merges or
replaces a populated ledger. This differs from the Web create-and-import flow.
After reviewing counts/warnings and accepting the limitations, replace
SHA256_FROM_PREVIEW with the exact SHA-256 fingerprint from that preview:
  whab migration-example import ynab commit '~/Downloads/export.zip' --currency USD --fingerprint SHA256_FROM_PREVIEW
Inspect budgetId, counts and alreadyImported. Commit verifies the fingerprint,
previews again with the active parser and saves the import atomically. A changed
file/parser or nonempty destination is refused; no automatic write retry occurs.
If the result is uncertain, preview the SAME file in the SAME budget and inspect
alreadyImported and account list. If alreadyImported is true, verify the saved
result instead of creating another budget or a new import. Otherwise inspect
canImport/reason and the ledger before deciding whether to deliberately retry
the same reviewed fingerprint. Preserve the original file; do not reset a
budget, alter private storage or infer failure merely from a lost response.

3. Classify each imported account with the user's confirmed choice
Purpose: supply type/subtype and envelope-versus-tracking scope absent from the
YNAB dump. All imported accounts start as unclassified, off-budget accounts.
  whab migration-example account list --unclassified --format table
  whab migration-example account show "Example Card"
  whab migration-example account classify --help
Ask the user about ONE account's type, optional subtype and on-budget versus
off-budget scope. Do not infer these choices from its name, transaction
categories or register-derived balance estimate. Only after confirmation:
  whab migration-example account classify "Example Card" --type credit --subtype credit_card --on-budget
  whab migration-example account show "Example Card"
For a separately confirmed tracking investment, replace the name/ID explicitly:
  whab migration-example account classify WHAB_ACCOUNT_ID --type investment --subtype brokerage --off-budget
Check saved id/name, type, subtype, onBudget and unclassified in the result,
then repeat list/show for the next account. Names resolve uniquely or fail;
use exact stable IDs to disambiguate. JSON is the default and retains full IDs.
Only depository and credit support on-budget scope. Omitting scope preserves
it, so type=credit alone leaves an imported off-budget account off budget.
Classification preserves identity/history/annotations and requests no bank
sync. It does not verify imported balances. Revisions and request IDs are
handled internally. After an uncertain classification, run account show above
and inspect history:
  whab migration-example history list
Retain the reported intent; do not rerun classify as a blind retry.
Also ask whether an account is OPEN or CLOSED; off-budget does not mean closed.
A user-confirmed off-budget closed CD uses the canonical deposit/cd classification:
  whab migration-example account classify "Example CD" --type deposit --subtype cd --off-budget
  whab migration-example account close "Example CD"
  whab migration-example account show "Example CD"
Closed accounts are archives: no new manual entries or bank updates. Closing
preserves historical treatment and uncertainty; it does not zero/verify balances.
Reopening is a separate confirmed choice:
  whab migration-example account reopen "Example CD"
It resumes configured history on a later normal sync; neither action starts sync.
Already classified accounts need no new decision unless the user requests it.

4. Optionally attach an existing shared Plaid connection
Purpose: reuse authorized bank access without creating duplicate bank logins.
Skip stages 4-6 and 8 if no bank imports are wanted.
  whab migration-example plugin enable plaid
  whab migration-example bank schedule plaid
While reviewing setup, explicitly choose Manual only for this destination if
agreed with the user; it suppresses periodic/webhook imports, keeps explicit
sync available and does not change other budgets' policies:
  whab migration-example bank schedule plaid --manual
  whab migration-example bank shared plaid
Inspect connections[].itemId, institution/profile, owner and every attachment,
plus unavailableBudgets. Choose the correct observed itemId as CONNECTION_ID.
Existing budget attachments must stay intact. Report unavailableBudgets: an
incomplete discovery cannot prove that every connection/attachment was reviewed.
Verify the chosen connection before sharing; global disconnection requires a
complete affected-budget review. After the user confirms sharing that existing
connection with this destination:
  whab migration-example bank attach plaid --item CONNECTION_ID
  whab migration-example bank shared plaid
Verify the destination's attached status and the other budgets' retained
attachments. Attachment alone does not import transactions or open bank login.
If already attached, continue from its existing mappings rather than reset it.
If there is no suitable connection, new bank consent/login is interactive in
Plaid Web settings; there is no CLI shortcut that creates consent. Do not
replace existing connections. Detach removes only this budget's attachment
and retains its history; global disconnect revokes access for ALL attached
budgets. Neither action is a migration prerequisite. Sharing stays within the
selected runtime/environment; never copy tokens or runtime metadata.

5. Preview provider accounts and save an explicitly reviewed mapping
Purpose: send future bank imports to the correct imported WHAB accounts with
an explicit history choice for EACH bank account.
  whab migration-example bank preview plaid --item CONNECTION_ID
  whab migration-example account list
Preview calls the provider but imports no transactions and advances no sync
cursor; it can refresh safe discovery metadata. Read accounts[].id/name/mask/
currency/link and destinations[].id/name/type/available/latestDate. The provider
accounts[].id becomes BANK_ACCOUNT_ID. The imported WHAB account's stable id
from account list/destinations becomes WHAB_ACCOUNT_ID. Confirm each mapping
with the user, using identities/currency/asset-versus-debt compatibility; an
unclassified destination must be classified before configuring. Closed archives
are intentionally unavailable as NEW destinations: omit those provider accounts
rather than reopening them just to link. Existing archived mappings stay paused.

Choose each inclusive start date deliberately. 2026-01-01 below is FICTIONAL:
replace it with that account's user-confirmed YYYY-MM-DD date. Never derive a
cutoff automatically from latestDate or the latest YNAB transaction. The
alternative since:null means an explicit choice of ALL AVAILABLE HISTORY;
it cannot fetch history beyond the provider/institution's availability.
The JSON array must contain the complete selection for this connection in
this budget: one object per selected provider account, with all three fields.
Omitted provider accounts are skipped; at least one selection is required.
Existing selections are replaced, so retain every previously intended row.
Example A (one account, explicit inclusive date):
  whab migration-example bank configure plaid --item CONNECTION_ID --accounts '[{"bankAccountId":"BANK_ACCOUNT_ID","accountId":"WHAB_ACCOUNT_ID","since":"2026-01-01"}]'
Example B is an ALTERNATIVE for explicitly chosen all-available history;
do not run both examples blindly:
  whab migration-example bank configure plaid --item CONNECTION_ID --accounts '[{"bankAccountId":"BANK_ACCOUNT_ID","accountId":"WHAB_ACCOUNT_ID","since":null}]'
Use accountId:null only when the user deliberately wants a NEW WHAB account,
not when an imported account is the intended destination. Configure saves
mapping/history settings and may refresh provider account metadata/balances;
it does not import transaction changes. A previously explicit destination
cannot silently be changed to a different account. Earlier cutoffs reset the
provider cursor for replay; existing history before a cutoff is retained.
Review configured/retiredAccounts, then verify every saved link and since:
  whab migration-example bank preview plaid --item CONNECTION_ID
Do not continue with missing/wrong/excluded links. Configuration and sync are
separate writes. For a failed/uncertain configure or attach, inspect shared,
preview and current accounts before deciding whether any retry is needed.

6. Review the saved plan, then explicitly sync
Purpose: import only the chosen provider accounts/history after review.
Confirm connection, destinations, exclusions and each date/null choice in the
fresh preview. Overlapping YNAB/Plaid records are NOT automatically matched or
deduplicated; stable Plaid IDs prevent duplicate provider replays, not overlap
with the YNAB import. A date alone does not guarantee zero overlap or no gaps.
Resolve that history decision with the user before requesting:
  whab migration-example bank sync plaid --item CONNECTION_ID
Inspect added/modified/removed counts and any errors. No automatic CLI replay
occurs. An uncertain sync is not proof that nothing was saved: inspect accounts,
connections, available transaction views and schedule status before deciding
on another explicit sync. Do not reset cursors, edit databases or submit an
unreviewed wider history window to resolve uncertainty.

7. Verify the migrated result and its financial limits
Purpose: check what was saved without claiming a reconciled YNAB clone.
  whab migration-example account list --format table
  whab migration-example account show "Example Card"
  whab migration-example bank connections plaid
  whab migration-example trnx non-reviewed
  whab migration-example trnx uncategorized --limit 10 --format table
  whab migration-example insights summary
Omit bank connections when Plaid was skipped. Inspect account identities,
classifications, scope, mappings and the public balanceUnknown/stale/source
fields in default JSON account output. Compare import counts with the reviewed
export and sync counts with the chosen plan. Review notes/categories/reviews,
duplicates/gaps and any excluded accounts. The transaction commands above are
FILTERED lists: non-reviewed excludes reviewed/deleted rows; uncategorized
shows only rows with no category, and --limit is a sample. Neither proves that
all imported transactions are present. Use the optional Web register to inspect
the complete selected account/date range when a full register review is needed.

Summary defaults to the current month and USD; choose --month YYYY-MM and
--currency USD explicitly when reviewing a different month. Verify the returned
budgetId and scope; JSON amounts are integer currency minor units. Imported
register-derived balances remain unverified estimates and are excluded from
spendable funding/net-worth calculations until a supported known snapshot
exists. Classification does not verify them; provider snapshots also are not
an audited reconciliation. The dump omits account type/scope, verified balances,
currency metadata, closed status, targets and scheduled transactions. Flags and
clearing status remain in notes; exported split lines stay separate. WHAB
recalculates envelope activity/availability from its own ledger: YNAB credit-card
payment envelopes, rollover and Ready to Assign totals can differ. Reconcile
these decisions with the user rather than declaring exact YNAB equivalence.
Completion means reviewed saved data and accepted limits, not proof of bank
balance correctness or perfect credit-card/rollover equivalence.

8. Choose ongoing updates; six-hour example
Purpose: make automatic bank-import frequency an explicit user choice AFTER
verification. This policy is per budget/provider and covers its attached
connections. It retains the chosen mappings and per-account history starts.
  whab migration-example bank schedule plaid --every-hours 6
  whab migration-example bank schedule plaid
Inspect jobs, interval_seconds=21600, due/last-attempt/success/error information
as returned. Every six hours is the example, not hourly. Checks run while WHAB
is running; a short-lived CLI host does not stay awake just because a cadence
was saved. To choose manual imports instead (suppressing periodic and webhook
imports while retaining explicit sync):
  whab migration-example bank schedule plaid --manual
Do not run that alternative if the user chose six-hour updates.

Optional background wakeups are a SEPARATE device/environment decision, not a
per-account or per-budget six-hour timer. On macOS only, after confirmation:
  whab migration-example bank background plaid --enable
  whab migration-example bank schedule plaid
Hourly launchd wakeups run due-job checks in the selected runtime home and
environment, including eligible jobs for other budgets/providers there. Each
budget/provider's saved cadence decides which imports are due; hourly wakeups
do not turn a six-hour cadence into hourly imports. Missed checks coalesce.
To unregister these shared runtime/environment wakeups:
  whab migration-example bank background plaid --disable
This does not change saved budget cadences; running hosts still check due jobs.
Other operating systems need their separately documented OS scheduler setup;
this CLI does not register background wakeups there. Never enable or alter
production scheduling as a development test. Verify the final schedule and
background status, with all user choices and remaining limits recorded.

Review semantics in WHAB 2.73 / YNAB 1.5:
Reviewed transactions require a valid category. No category means uncategorized and non-reviewed. Assigning a category alone never marks reviewed; clearing it also clears review. Explicit reviewed=true without a category rejects the entire operation before mutation. Transfer and Income are protected system categories with stable currency-scoped IDs (whab-system:transfer:USD and whab-system:income:USD), canonical systemKind metadata and target zero; they are selectable transaction classifications, not assignable expense envelopes. User categories with the same display names keep their own identities; ambiguous names require an exact ID or full path. Amount signs alone never classify Income. Imported clearing and category-agent labels do not establish a human reviewer's identity.
YNAB Transfer : rows with no expense category become System / Transfer. Explicit Inflow: Ready to Assign / Inflow: To be Budgeted rows become System / Income. Blank inflows remain uncategorized and non-reviewed. Flags and clearing stay in notes; no reviewer identity is inferred. Verify complete history with whab migration-example trnx list, then use trnx review --help for deliberate review. SQLite/JSON 1.24/1.16 with WHAB 2.73 correct current state when a writable primary opens or an old portable ledger is restored. Legacy explicit transfer flags become System / Transfer; other reviewed-but-uncategorized live records become non-reviewed. Existing user classifications, valid reviews, financial values and provider state remain unchanged. Blank historic inflows lack authoritative Income provenance and remain uncategorized; their previous funding calculation remains compatible. Immutable historical events and request receipts remain exact; a non-reversible system migration entry records every correction. Reopening is idempotent. Native transactions/replacement keep interruption recovery atomic. Do not downgrade migrated native files into an older installation: restore its matching private backup instead. Disabled/unavailable plugin payloads remain opaque and migrate only through their owning supported writable primary; fenced copies cannot accept correction independently.

input.description: Offline workflow documentation topic, not executable input. Follow the staged CLI commands in the guide.

output.description: Ordered migration guidance rendered from this packaged summary by plugin and import help. No operation is executed.

examples.output: Review one stage at a time; replace fictional budget, file, date, fingerprint and ID placeholders before any write.

operations.side_effects: Displaying this guide has no effects and opens no host. Its explicitly selected CLI commands separately create/import/classify/attach/configure/sync/schedule within their documented scopes. Bank login consent remains interactive.
operations.permissions: Offline installed documentation, without credentials, a profile, network access or plugin hooks. Executing each chosen command requires its normal verified local host access and user-confirmed decisions.
operations.scope: One explicitly name/ID-addressed permanent budget. Bank schedule is budget/provider scoped; optional background wakeups are runtime-home/environment scoped. Existing shared connection attachments in other budgets are preserved.
errors: Missing/ambiguous names, populated import destinations, changed fingerprints, invalid classifications or incompatible bank mappings are refused by their owning commands.
Uncertain results require inspection; never reset/reimport or blindly replay a mutation. Provider availability and YNAB export limitations remain material.
operations.retry: Help can be repeated safely. Resume migration from the verified actual stage. For uncertain writes, use the per-stage inspection/reconciliation guidance and preserve the original intent/fingerprint; no automatic mutation replay.
operations.availability: Documentation topic only, not a callable SDK or CLI operation. WHAB 2.64+, CLI 2.10+ (optional bank stages require Plaid 1.8+): whab BUDGET import ynab-zip-importer --help (ynab alias accepted), preview/commit --help; whab api describe --plugin ynab-zip-importer --help or --operation import.workflow --help. JSON: whab api describe --offline --plugin ynab-zip-importer --operation import.workflow --json.

operations.name: FileImport.parse
operations.summary: Parse supplied file bytes into a validated import preview; no automatic migration.

data.description: Supplied archive/file bytes, represented as base64.

output.description: The operation result in the enclosing response data field.

operations.side_effects: Parsing creates a preview. Applying a migration is a separate guarded host action.
operations.permissions: Host-scoped SDK access; this callback is not remotely callable.
operations.scope: Host-supplied budget/environment context and personal/demo workspace where the method accepts it. Credentials remain machine-local.
errors: Invalid or unsupported input is rejected without applying a new decision.
Unavailable feature/storage returns an authored error; stale revisions and reused request IDs with different intent conflict.

Invalid text encoding reports the decoder and byte offset without table contents; malformed tables and unsupported ZIP compression have authored diagnostics. Complete UTF-8 surrogate pairs are normalized losslessly; lone surrogates and other invalid bytes are rejected without guessing a legacy encoding or dropping text.
operations.retry: Read again as needed; reads never authorize a later write using an old revision.
operations.availability: SDK callback only; consult the owning README for the typed in-process contract.
